item.title: Dave Lee: Anthropic Brings ‘Anti-Sell’ Strategy to Its IPO
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Oct 26th, 2026
Dave Lee: Anthropic Brings ‘Anti-Sell’ Strategy to Its IPO
Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion US Technology Columnist, joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss his piece about Anthropic's IPO announcement. Lee writes about the firm's S-1 containing warnings about the company and prospects for humanity as AI technology continues to advance. Lee adds that the filing is described as “a pitch deliberately designed to be unappealing to those who are a poor fit … while appealing to the type of person we want to hire.” Lee speaks with Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.

Asian stocks were set to rise, tracking gains on Wall Street as Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering filing revived enthusiasm for artificial intelligence ahead of big tech earnings and the Federal Reserve’s rate decision.
Equity-index futures for Japan and South Korea pointed higher, while those for Australia were little changed. US stock contracts edged up in early Asian trading after the S&P 500 gained 0.7% and the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.1%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 2.8%, its biggest gain since Sept. 21.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Anthropic PBC warned it may need to seek more financing sooner than the artificial-intelligence company had anticipated while saying little about its potential path to an investment-grade credit rating in its closely watched IPO filing.
Reaching investment grade could give the maker of Claude access to a much deeper pool of capital at a time when its funding requirements are ballooning. Insurance companies, pension funds and other large investors are major buyers of high-grade corporate bonds, and attaining those ratings could allow Anthropic to borrow more cheaply.

item.title: Duke’s Mayo CEO: Our Room for Growth Is Substantial
item.description:
Oct 26th, 2026
Duke’s Mayo CEO: Our Room for Growth Is Substantial
E. Yuri Hermida, CEO of Duke’s Mayo Company, discussed the company’s name change from Sauer Brands as it enters a new growth chapter. After divesting its spice business, the company is centering its identity on Duke’s Mayo, whose heritage and recipe date to 1917, while also owning Mateo’s Gourmet Salsa. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close."

Colombia sold a record $5.2 billion in dollar-denominated bonds on Monday as a new administration pledges to rein in the widening budget gap and put the nation’s debt back on a sustainable path.
The nation pricedBloomberg Terminal
bonds due in 2032, 2037 and 2056 to yield 7.05%, 7.65% and 8.15%, respectively, down from initial price talks, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified. The deal would top the $4.95 billion in global debt sold back in January.

Nucor Corp. reported third-quarter earnings that beat Wall Street expectations as higher steel prices helped boost profits at the largest US steelmaker.
The Charlotte, North Carolina-based company posted earnings of $5.80 a share, slightly above the $5.77 average estimate of analysts surveyed by Bloomberg. Net sales were $11.2 billion, topping expectations for $10.8 billion.

item.title: Schwab CEO Says It's Easy to Find Top Talent in Texas
item.description: Schwab Corp. Chief Executive Officer Rick Wurster says Texas' cost of living, strong universities and tax advantages versus other states have helped the Westlake-based company recruit employees since relocating from San Francisco in 2021. Schwab now has almost 11,000 Texas employees, he tells Bloomberg's Julie Fine. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Week | High Stakes Summit, New Zealand's Brain Drain, Stablecoin Adoption, Bubbly Water
item.description: This week, China thinks it's cracked the code on Trump heading into a summit in Beijing. And, what happens when a country's best and brightest travel overseas and stop coming back? Plus, the most useful thing about crypto might be the one nobody's talking about: cheap and fast cross-border payments. Later, the smartest bet in the sparkling water boom might not be on any brand, but on the companies behind them. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Wall Street Week | Rerouting Global Trade, Private Equity Tested, Realizing Cuba’s Potential
item.description: This week, inflation may be edging lower, but as markets push rates higher, the Fed’s 2% inflation target might be a long way off. And, Mexico is building a land-based trade corridor that could give shipping companies more options when traditional channels are disrupted. Plus, as exits slow and borrowing costs rise, the ability of private equity investments to generate returns that beat public markets is less certain. Later, Cuba is promising its biggest market reforms in decades, but investors remain skeptical that the state will truly give up control. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: We Support Zuckerberg's Vision: Cassidy
item.description: Lauren Cassidy, CIO at Founders 100 ETF, joins Scarlet Fu and Athanasios Psarofagis on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." They discuss the Founders 100 ETF (ticker: FFF), the possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX, and how Meta is seeking to raise as much as $95B from selling common and preferred stock. (Source: Bloomberg)
